title: Around the World: Magellan & Elcano, 1519–1522
summary: Five ships and about 270 sailors left Spain to find a western route to the Spice Islands. Three years later, one ship and 18 men came home – the first voyage around the world.

moves.name: The search for the Spice Islands

events.title: The fleet sets sail
events.text: Five ships – Trinidad, San Antonio, Concepción, Victoria and Santiago – leave Sanlúcar de Barrameda.

events.title: Mutiny at San Julián
events.text: Three captains rebel during the long southern winter. Magellan crushes the mutiny.

events.title: Santiago wrecked
events.text: The smallest ship is lost while scouting the coast.

events.title: Entering the strait
events.text: The fleet finds the passage now called the Strait of Magellan. The San Antonio deserts and sails home.

events.title: The Pacific Ocean
events.text: Magellan names the calm ocean 'Mar Pacífico'. The crossing takes over three months; many sailors die of scurvy.

events.title: Battle of Mactan
events.text: Magellan is killed fighting Lapulapu's warriors on Mactan island.

events.title: Spice Islands reached
events.text: The ships load cloves at Tidore in the Moluccas – the goal of the voyage.

events.title: Rounding the Cape of Good Hope
events.text: Elcano avoids Portuguese ports and sails a dangerous route far from the coast.

events.title: Victoria returns
events.text: 18 survivors complete the first circumnavigation of the Earth.

story.title: A race for spices
story.text: In the 1500s, spices like **cloves and nutmeg** were worth more than gold in Europe – and they grew only in the Spice Islands (Moluccas). Portugal controlled the route around Africa, so **Ferdinand Magellan** offered Spain a daring idea: reach the islands by sailing **west**.

question.prompt: Why did Magellan sail west instead of around Africa?
choices: Portugal controlled the eastern route around Africa
The western route was already well known

story.title: Across the Atlantic
story.text: The fleet crossed the Atlantic to Brazil and sailed south along South America, searching every bay for a passage to the other ocean.

story.title: Winter and mutiny
story.text: At **San Julián** the crews spent a freezing winter. Some captains rebelled, wanting to go home. Magellan crushed the mutiny – and lost a ship in a storm.

story.title: The Strait of Magellan
story.text: In October 1520 the fleet found a narrow, winding passage through the tip of South America. It took **38 days** to get through – and one ship secretly turned back to Spain.

question.prompt: What is the passage at the tip of South America called today?
question.explain: The Panama Canal was only built in the 20th century.

story.title: The endless Pacific
story.text: Nobody in Europe knew how big the Pacific was. The crossing took **over three months**. Food ran out; sailors ate leather and sawdust, and many died of **scurvy**.

question.prompt: The goal of the voyage was the Spice Islands (the Moluccas). Click where they are.
question.explain: The Moluccas lie in today's Indonesia, between Sulawesi and New Guinea.

story.title: Death at Mactan
story.text: In the Philippines Magellan tried to force local rulers to accept Spanish rule and Christianity. On **27 April 1521** he was killed at **Mactan** by the warriors of chief **Lapulapu**.

question.prompt: Did Magellan himself complete the voyage around the world?
choices: Yes, he arrived back in Spain in 1522
No, he was killed in the Philippines in 1521
No, he turned back at the Strait

story.title: Elcano brings the Victoria home
story.text: With only one ship left, **Juan Sebastián Elcano** loaded cloves in the Moluccas and sailed home across the Indian Ocean and around Africa. On **6 September 1522**, 18 survivors reached Spain: the first people to sail around the world.

choices: The Earth can be sailed around, and the Pacific is enormous
question.explain: Educated Europeans already knew the Earth was round – the voyage showed how big it really is.

sources: Antonio Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (1524)
Laurence Bergreen, Over the Edge of the World (2003)
